data: This course introduces key directions and themes in feminist thought and practice, both global and local, spanning a time frame starting from the eighteenth century to the contemporary times. Examining how gender and sexuality operates in society, we examine how gender is not an individual attribute or a role, but rather a system of social practices that constructs different categories of people—“men” and “women”—and organizes social interaction and inequality around this difference. The course will take a sociological approach in understanding what is sex and gender , how they operate in the labor market, at home, and at school, and how they structure our everyday lives at the individual, interactional, and institutional level. Throughout the course, we will prioritize reading, evaluating, and questioning feminist theory and sociological research on gender. We will also investigate feminist thought from a variety of disciplinary perspectives and theoretical orientations and focus on key debates such as the sex/gender system, intersectionality, sexual difference, and essentialism, amongst others. This course aims to think through the ways in which gender and sexuality intersect with caste, class, community and the nation. The aim of this course is to unravel the centrality of power in the practice of gender.
